 Bangladesh lose to Scotland in Hong Kong Sixes opener
 After Scotland opted to field, Sabbir Rahman and Habibur Rahman Sohan opened the batting for Bangladesh. Sohan made an explosive start, smashing a six off the very first ball. He then gave Sabbir the strike, and the experienced batter also opened his account with a maximum.
 Written by : Khan Mutasim Billah Life 
 Posted - Oct 30, 2026, 10:47 am 2026-10-30T10:47:04+06:00 
 Updated - Oct 30, 2026, 10:47 am 2026-10-30T10:47:04+06:00 
 Bangladesh began their Hong Kong Sixes campaign with a defeat as they lost to Scotland in their opening match of the tournament. 
 After Scotland opted to field, Sabbir Rahman and Habibur Rahman Sohan opened the batting for Bangladesh. Sohan made an explosive start, smashing a six off the very first ball. He then gave Sabbir the strike, and the experienced batter also opened his account with a maximum.
 The two batters continued to clear the ropes in the opening over, which produced 26 runs. Sohan alone contributed 19 of those runs. His incredible start came to an end after just six balls, as he was caught by Jasper Davidson near the boundary. Sohan walked back after scoring 25, including four sixes.
 Get Latest Cricket Updates on WhatsApp Chowdhury Md Rizwan came in next and took a single off his first ball, bringing Sabbir back on strike. However, Sabbir tried to clear the boundary and was caught by a fielder. He scored eight off four deliveries.
 With Bangladesh under pressure, the responsibility fell on young batters Rizwan and Ahrar Amin Piyan. Neither could make much of an impact. Piyan scored 7 off 6 balls, while Rizwan managed just 3 from 6 deliveries. Bangladesh also went 13 balls without hitting a boundary during this period.
 After the fourth wicket fell with the score at 48, captain Abu Hider Rony tried to keep the innings going alongside Mrittunjoy Chowdhury . Rony played a quickfire knock of 25 off 9 balls before getting dismissed, leaving Mrittunjoy with little support at the other end.
 Mrittunjoy had to face the remaining deliveries almost single-handedly and finished unbeaten on 21 off 6 balls. Bangladesh ended their six overs at 94 for 5.
 Scotland made a strong start to the chase, scoring 19 runs in the first over. Mrittunjoy then bowled four consecutive dot balls at the start of the second over and put the batters under pressure.
 However, opener Finlay McCreath kept Scotland on track with an outstanding innings. He took control of the chase and brought his team within touching distance of victory.
 McCreath smashed 53 off just 20 balls. Under the Hong Kong Sixes rules, a batter must retire after scoring a half-century, so he had to leave the field after reaching the milestone.
 Scotland then showed some clever thinking. After Mackenzie Jones was dismissed, they declared their next two batters retired out and allowed McCreath to return to the crease.
 Follow google news channel to get news of BDCricTime. With four runs needed from the final ball, Jack Jarvis smashed a six to seal a thrilling victory for Scotland and leave Bangladesh disappointed in their opening match.
